question: Why did attempts to repeat Fleming's 1928 plate, by dropping mould spores onto bacteria, keep failing?
answer: Because penicillin kills only bacteria that are growing; established colonies shrug it off. Decades later Ronald Hare showed the mould had to get going first. A cool spell in London that summer let it spread while the staphylococci barely grew; warmer days then brought the bacteria up around a mould already making its drug.
move: When a lucky result will not repeat, ask what the conditions were that day.
reference: Hare, The Birth of Penicillin and the Disarming of Microbes, George Allen & Unwin, 1970
